summary: Wasco County, OR lookout site: rag camp 1927, tower c.1932, state-owned from 1950, removed after 1965; little remains per Oregon Hikers.

facts.design: Sources disagree: 10' wooden live-in tower (c.1932); 12' timber tower with 12x12 cab (1933); 8' wooden L-4 (1945)
facts.status_note: Removed per the Forest Lookouts history; FFLOS says it has since disappeared; little remains per Oregon Hikers, and an antenna stands on the butte
facts.agency: Oregon Department of Forestry (state ownership from 1950; built by the Mount Hood National Forest)

visit.trail_note: Postage Stamp Butte Loop, moderate, 4.4 mi, 780 ft gain, per Oregon Hikers; the guide quotes a former lookout on numerous large rattlesnakes in the area

events.note: Rag camp set up at the site
10-foot wooden live-in tower, about this date
Forest Lookouts history: 12-foot timber tower with 12x12 cab, built with CCC labor; differs from the 1932 tower in the other sources
State assumed ownership of the station
Station reported the White River #1 fire (September 9) and the White River #2 fire (September 15)
Cab replaced (FFLOS and firelookout.com); Forest Lookouts history says material from Lost Lake Butte lookout was salvaged for this site
Tower material bought, pre-cut and sent for treatment
No first reports called in from the station during fire season; the page then lists the lookout as removed, with no date
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on September 20, 2010

sources.title: Postage Stamp Butte Fire Lookout Tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give a 10-foot live-in tower (about 1932), a 12-foot timber tower with 12x12 cab (1933), and an 8-foot L-4 (1945). The record's 3.7 m height matches only the 12-foot tower; we kept it with this caveat.

The Former Fire Lookout Sites register and firelookout.com say the cab was replaced in 1963. The Forest Lookouts history says material from the Lost Lake Butte lookout was salvaged for this site, with pre-cut material bought in 1964.

notes_for_editor: Tower design and dates conflict across three sources. No source describes what remains at the site beyond the Oregon Hikers note of little remaining and an antenna. No source states public access; the hiking guide describes a loop that reaches the site, so access is left out of facts. Fate: removed after the 1965 entry, undated.
